What happens when water hits a SUPER hot pan? Instead of evaporating instantly, it floats, dances, and survives far longer than it should. This counterintuitive phenomenon is called the Leidenfrost effect — and the physics behind it will blow your mind.
In this video, we explain the Leidenfrost effect in simple words: how a tiny vapor cushion forms between the water droplet and the scorching surface, why this makes the droplet hover like a hovercraft, and the real-world applications from blacksmithing to steel manufacturing to lava flowing into the ocean.
